correctness.rationale: Positive shift weights give |W| diagonal and ordinary unilateral polar shift, so one Aluthge transform sends log w_j to (1-t)log w_j+t log w_{j+1}; after n iterates log w_j^(n)=E log w_{j+B_n} for Bin(n,t). Monotonicity guarantees these are the decreasing singular-value list, not merely unordered weights. Uniform regular variation on compact positive index ratios [t/2,R+1] coupled with exponential Chernoff concentration proves the macroscopic profile (t+u)^-β uniformly 0<=u<=R; the exceptional contribution is O(log n e^-cn) using monotonicity. The counting law follows from the unique crossing of (1+u/t)^-β with θ. For βp>1, the integral ∫0^∞(t+u)^-βp du=t^{1-βp}/(βp-1) follows from Riemann sums plus a Potter bound on the infinite tail, rather than finite approximation; ideal membership equivalence w_{j+n}<=w_j^(n)<=w_j is correct including the critical slowly varying case. Independently checked numerical log-binomial smoothing for nonconstant slowly varying L(j)=log(j+e)^0.65, β=1.2, t=.35, ranks j up to 3n for n=100,400,1000; norm ratios approach predicted t^-β and maximum local errors decrease (0.555,0.419,0.360), consistent but not proof.
